lines.en: Lia, you look exhausted. Have you been sleeping badly, or have you been working late again this week?
lines.pt: Lia, você parece exausta. Tem dormido mal, ou tem trabalhado até tarde de novo esta semana?

lines.en: Both. I’ve been looking for a better job for three months, and I’ve been updating my résumé every night.
lines.pt: Os dois. Estou procurando um emprego melhor há três meses e tenho atualizado meu currículo toda noite.

lines.en: Three months! I didn’t know. Have you been talking to any headhunters, or have you only been applying online?
lines.pt: Três meses! Eu não sabia. Tem conversado com algum headhunter, ou só tem se candidatado pela internet?

lines.en: Both again. A headhunter has been calling me since March, and I’ve been going to interviews on my lunch breaks.
lines.pt: De novo os dois. Um headhunter tem me ligado desde março, e tenho ido a entrevistas na hora do almoço.

lines.en: That explains it. I’ve noticed you’ve been disappearing at noon. Why have you been so unhappy here, honestly?
lines.pt: Isso explica. Notei que você tem sumido ao meio-dia. Por que tem estado tão infeliz aqui, sinceramente?

lines.en: The workload has been growing for a year, and nobody has been listening. I’ve been dealing with burnout since January.
lines.pt: A carga de trabalho vem crescendo há um ano, e ninguém tem escutado. Lido com o esgotamento desde janeiro.

lines.en: I’m sorry. I’ve been thinking about the same thing, actually. My commute has been getting longer and my salary has not been rising.
lines.pt: Sinto muito. Na verdade, tenho pensado na mesma coisa. Meu trajeto tem ficado mais longo e meu salário não tem subido.

lines.en: Then we’ve both been waiting too long. How long have you been thinking about leaving?
lines.pt: Então nós dois temos esperado demais. Há quanto tempo você pensa em sair?

lines.en: Since the spring. But I haven’t been brave enough to start. Have you heard back from the company in Chicago?
lines.pt: Desde a primavera. Mas não tive coragem de começar. Já teve resposta da empresa de Chicago?

lines.en: Not yet. They’ve been reviewing the shortlist all week. I’ve been checking my phone every ten minutes.
lines.pt: Ainda não. Eles têm analisado a lista final a semana toda. Tenho olhado o celular a cada dez minutos.

lines.en: Send me your résumé tonight. I’ve been meaning to start, and I’d love your advice on how you’ve been preparing.
lines.pt: Me mande seu currículo hoje à noite. Venho querendo começar, e adoraria seu conselho sobre como você tem se preparado.

facts.label: Present perfect contínuo
facts.sub: Ação que começou antes e continua: I’ve been looking for a job since March. Pergunta: How long have you been…? Use for/since.

facts.label: Ação em curso
facts.sub: Use have/has been + verbo com -ing para algo que começou antes e continua agora: I’ve been looking for a job. Com for e since você informa a duração. Ele enfatiza o processo, não só o resultado.

facts.label: Duração
facts.sub: For + período: for three months. Since + ponto de partida: since March. Em português usamos “há” para ambos. Nunca use o presente simples: diga I’ve been working here since 2019.

pages.title: A quiet job hunt · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey Thursday morning in Boston. The open-plan office is quiet and tense. Boris notices that Lia looks very tired. She has been leaving at noon for weeks. Something is clearly going on. Over coffee, the truth finally comes out.

“Lia, you look exhausted. Have you been sleeping badly, or have you been working late again this week?” says Boris. “Both. I’ve been looking for a better job for three months, and I’ve been updating my résumé every night.” says Lia. “Three months! I didn’t know. Have you been talking to any headhunters, or have you only been applying online?” says Boris.

pages.title: Encontre a frase natural

opts: I look for a job since March.
I’ve been looking for a job since March.
I am looking for a job since March.
items.why: Use have been + -ing with since, not the present simple or continuous.

opts: She has been work here for years.
She has been working here for years.
She has be working here for years.
items.why: After have/has been, the verb takes -ing.

opts: How long have you been waiting?
items.why: Ask with How long + have you been + -ing.

opts: I have been know him for years.
I have been knowing him for years.
I have known him for years.
items.why: Stative verbs like know do not take the continuous form.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Escolha a frase mais natural. → I’ve been looking for a job since March.
Escolha a frase mais natural. → She has been working here for years.
Escolha a frase mais natural. → How long have you been waiting?
Escolha a frase mais natural. → I have known him for years.
